reason: A is more physically defensible because it focuses on alloy-, defect-, and oxygen-induced scattering without B’s unsupported claims that weak localization dominates up to 200 K or that bulk interstitial oxygen causes oxidation-state effects. Both lack a genuinely held-out conductivity benchmark and strong supporting evidence, but B additionally calibrates on conductivity data it proposes to test against and cites evidence largely unrelated to conductivity.
